title: NEOWISE does not establish an infrared dip signal for the field-dwarf candidate G3461
abstract: We test the infrared history of Gaia DR3 346100804155947392, a field-dwarf dimmer candidate found by a PS1 versus Gaia XP epoch survey. A new reduction uses 21 NEOWISE visits, ten local controls and ZTF DR24. With an offset for each scan season, eleven five-day optical matches give a W1 response of 0.124 +/- 0.064 mag per r mag and a W2 response of -0.036 +/- 0.124. Seven one-day matches give 0.015 +/- 0.078 and -0.068 +/- 0.210. These are conditional regression errors. Neither test establishes a positive infrared dip signal. Only 26.5 percent of target W1 detections pass a strict profile-fit chi2 cut; this leaves one optical match. A weak early-to-late W1 change also loses precision under this cut. Thus the archive data do not independently confirm dust for this candidate. They do not exclude dust, spots, blending or changing emission. No grain size or stellar age is measured. The package preserves original code, aggregate evidence, figures, checks and exact external-input provenance.

display.caption: The conditional infrared response changes with optical timing and fit quality. Neither band has a stable positive dip detection.
Optical nightly depths and infrared visits have very different time sampling.
